desc: Mumbai High is the largest offshore oil field in India, located about 160 km west of Mumbai in the Arabian Sea. Discovered in 1974 by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), it began production in 1976. The field accounts for a significant portion of India's domestic crude oil and natural gas production. It operates through a network of platforms including the iconic Bombay High Platform. The field is in water depths of about 75 meters and has over 300 wells.
fact: It is the largest offshore oil field in India, discovered in 1974 · It accounts for a major share of India's domestic crude oil production · It operates through over 300 wells on multiple platforms · It is located 160 km west of Mumbai in the Arabian Sea

desc: Krishna Godavari (KG) Basin is one of India's most significant oil and gas basins, located offshore of Andhra Pradesh along the Bay of Bengal coast. The basin gained international attention with the discovery of the D6 block by Reliance Industries in 2002, one of the largest gas discoveries in the world. The basin covers an area of about 15,000 km² in the deltaic and offshore regions. It has substantial natural gas reserves and contributes significantly to India's domestic gas production. The basin also contains significant oil discoveries and continues to be explored.
fact: The KG Basin D6 block discovery by Reliance in 2002 was among the largest gas discoveries in the world · The basin covers 15,000 km² offshore Andhra Pradesh · It contributes significantly to India's domestic natural gas production · The basin continues to be actively explored for both oil and gas

desc: Mangala Oil Field is the largest onshore oil field in India, located in the Barmer district of Rajasthan. Discovered in 2004 by Cairn India (now Vedanta), it began production in 2009. The field is part of the Barmer Basin and produces high-quality, sweet crude oil suitable for refining into high-value products. It utilizes enhanced oil recovery techniques including hot water injection to maximize production. The oil is transported via a 590 km heated pipeline to the Salaya-Mundra refinery in Gujarat. The field has over 300 producing wells and has been a transformative asset for India's energy security.
fact: Mangala is the largest onshore oil field in India, discovered in 2004 · It uses enhanced oil recovery with hot water injection · Oil is transported via a 590 km heated pipeline to Gujarat · The field has over 300 producing wells in the Barmer Basin, Rajasthan

desc: Digboi Oil Field is the oldest oil field in India and one of the oldest still-producing oil fields in the world, located in the Tinsukia district of Assam. Oil was first struck at Digboi in 1889, and production began in 1901. The field is operated by Oil India Limited and has produced oil continuously for over a century. The Digboi Refinery, established in 1901, is the oldest operating refinery in Asia. The field is located in the Assam-Arakan Basin and produces waxy crude oil from multiple Eocene-aged sandstone reservoirs.
fact: Digboi is the oldest oil field in India, producing since 1901 · The Digboi Refinery established in 1901 is the oldest operating refinery in Asia · It is located in the Assam-Arakan Basin, Tinsukia district · It has produced oil continuously for over 120 years

desc: Ankleshwar Oil Field is a major onshore oil field located in the Bharuch district of Gujarat, within the Cambay Basin. Discovered in 1958, it played a pivotal role in establishing India's domestic oil production before the discovery of Mumbai High. The field is operated by ONGC and produces from multiple reservoir layers in Eocene and Oligocene formations. It has been under production for over six decades and continues to contribute to Gujarat's oil output. The field is part of the larger Cambay Basin which is one of India's most prolific onshore hydrocarbon provinces.
fact: Ankleshwar was a pivotal discovery in 1958 that established India's onshore oil production · It is located in the Cambay Basin, Bharuch district, Gujarat · It has been under production for over 65 years · It produces from multiple Eocene and Oligocene reservoir layers

desc: The Cambay Basin is a major hydrocarbon province in Gujarat, extending from Surat to Sanchor and covering an area of about 56,000 km². It is one of India's most important onshore oil and gas basins, discovered in 1958. The basin contains multiple fields including Ankleshwar, Kalol, Gandhar, and Sanand. It produces both oil and natural gas from Eocene and Oligocene reservoirs. The basin has been extensively explored and developed by ONGC and continues to contribute significantly to Gujarat's energy production, supporting the state's extensive petrochemical and refining infrastructure.
fact: The Cambay Basin is one of India's most important onshore hydrocarbon provinces covering 56,000 km² · It contains multiple fields including Ankleshwar, Kalol, Gandhar, and Sanand · Discovered in 1958, it produces from Eocene and Oligocene reservoirs · It supports Gujarat's extensive petrochemical and refining infrastructure
